components.note: 骨 (bone) — 骨 is the bone radical, as in 骼, 髓, 体; 骨 is bones, with ⺼ (flesh) beneath.
扌 (hand) — hand radical — 折 shows a hand swinging an axe 斤, so to chop or snap, then to fold and bend.
斤 (axe) — 斤 is an axe, as in 析 and 新; it is the cutting tool.

example.hanzi: 他滑雪时不小心骨折了。
example.pinyin: Tā huáxuě shí bùxiǎoxīn gǔzhé le.
example.english: He accidentally broke a bone while skiing.
example.fact: The human body has 206 bones in adulthood but starts life with about 270 to 300 at birth, because many bones — like the skull plates and parts of the spine — begin as separate pieces of cartilage or bone that fuse together as a child grows, which is also why fractures in children often heal faster than in adults.

examples.hanzi: 她骨折了，要在家休息两个月。
examples.pinyin: Tā gǔzhé le, yào zài jiā xiūxi liǎng ge yuè.
examples.english: She broke a bone and has to rest at home for two months.

examples.hanzi: 这次骨折让他不能踢球了。
examples.pinyin: Zhè cì gǔzhé ràng tā bù néng tī qiú le.
examples.english: This fracture means he can't play soccer.

components.note: 扌 (hand radical, 提手旁) — actions by hand: 打, 拉, 抱; here a hand seizing someone to pass judgment.
卩 (kneeling person) — with 又 hand: sentencing a kneeling prisoner, then answering back: repay, report.
亻 (person) — marks people, as in 你, 他, 做; 仇 is an enemy, a person you hate.
九 (jiǔ) is only a loose sound hint for chóu.

example.hanzi: 他花了十年时间才为父亲报仇。
example.pinyin: Tā huā le shí nián shíjiān cái wèi fùqīn bàochóu.
example.english: It took him ten years to finally avenge his father.
example.fact: The Count of Monte Cristo, Alexandre Dumas's 1844 novel of imprisonment and elaborate revenge, was partly inspired by a real police file Dumas encountered about François Picaud, a Frenchman falsely imprisoned by jealous friends who spent years methodically ruining each of their lives after his release.

examples.hanzi: 他发誓要为朋友报仇。
examples.pinyin: Tā fāshì yào wèi péngyou bàochóu.
examples.english: He swore to take revenge for his friend.

examples.hanzi: 电影里的主角一心想报仇。
examples.pinyin: Diànyǐng lǐ de zhǔjué yìxīn xiǎng bàochóu.
examples.english: The hero in the movie is set on revenge.

components.note: 虫 (insect) — small creatures, as in 蛇 snake, 蚊 mosquito, 蝴蝶 butterfly.
扁 (biǎn) gives a close sound; it also sounds out 编 biān and 篇 piān.
虫 (insect) — small creatures, as in 蛇 snake, 蚊 mosquito.
畐 (fú) gives the exact sound; it also sounds out 福 fú. Bats are lucky in China since 蝠 sounds like 福 fortune.

example.hanzi: 蝙蝠在夜里靠回声定位捕食。
example.pinyin: Biānfú zài yèlǐ kào huíshēng dìngwèi bǔshí.
example.english: Bats hunt at night using echolocation.
example.fact: Bats are the only mammals capable of true, sustained flight, and many species navigate and hunt in complete darkness using echolocation — emitting high-frequency calls, some above 100 kHz, and interpreting the returning echoes with enough precision to detect an insect the width of a human hair in midair.

examples.hanzi: 蝙蝠白天睡觉，晚上出来活动。
examples.pinyin: Biānfú báitiān shuìjiào, wǎnshang chūlái huódòng.
examples.english: Bats sleep during the day and come out at night.

examples.hanzi: 山洞里住着很多蝙蝠。
examples.pinyin: Shāndòng lǐ zhùzhe hěn duō biānfú.
examples.english: Many bats live in the cave.

components.note: 玉 (jade) — jade put away safely: 全 first meant flawless, pure, then whole.
宀 (roof) — houses and shelter, as in 室 room, 安 safe, 字 character; 家 is home.
豕 (pig) — a pig under a roof: pigs were kept in the home, hence home and family.

example.hanzi: 全家人一起去海边度假。
example.pinyin: Quánjiā rén yīqǐ qù hǎibiān dùjià.
example.english: The whole family went to the seaside for vacation together.
example.fact: China's Spring Festival travel period, when hundreds of millions of people journey home to reunite with family for the Lunar New Year, is the largest annual human migration on Earth — in recent years, total trips during the roughly 40-day travel window have exceeded 2 billion, more than the population of every country except China and India combined.

examples.hanzi: 春节的时候，全家都会聚在一起。
examples.pinyin: Chūnjié de shíhou, quánjiā dōu huì jù zài yìqǐ.
examples.english: At Spring Festival, the whole family gets together.

examples.hanzi: 我们全家都喜欢吃辣的。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen quánjiā dōu xǐhuan chī là de.
examples.english: My whole family likes spicy food.

components.note: 示 (altar, ritual) — 示 (礻 on the left side) marks rites and the sacred, as in 神, 礼, 福; 禁 is taboo, then forbidden.
林 (lín) — near sound — 禁 is jìn; 林 also sounds out 襟 jīn.

example.hanzi: 这里禁止吸烟。
example.pinyin: Zhèlǐ jìnzhǐ xīyān.
example.english: Smoking is prohibited here.
example.fact: 禁止 is the standard word on "no" signs: 禁止吸烟 (no smoking). The same character has a second reading jīn meaning "to endure," in 禁不住 and 不禁. 紫禁城 (the Forbidden City) uses it too.

examples.hanzi: 图书馆里禁止大声说话。
examples.pinyin: Túshūguǎn lǐ jìnzhǐ dàshēng shuōhuà.
examples.english: Talking loudly is forbidden in the library.

examples.hanzi: 这条路晚上禁行。
examples.pinyin: Zhè tiáo lù wǎnshang jìnxíng.
examples.english: This road is closed to traffic at night.

components.note: 日 (sun) — spring is when the sun warms and plants sprout; also in 明 bright, 时 time.
大 (big person) — a person with a line above the head, marking the sky above; tiān = heaven, sky, day.

example.hanzi: 春天到了,花都开了。
example.pinyin: Chūntiān dào le, huā dōu kāi le.
example.english: Spring has arrived, and all the flowers are blooming.
example.fact: Japan's cherry blossom season, celebrated in the tradition of hanami, typically lasts only about one to two weeks per location, and meteorologists track the 'blossom front' as it moves northward across the country each spring — the Japan Meteorological Agency has published official forecasts for peak bloom dates since 1951.

examples.hanzi: 春天的公园里到处是花。
examples.pinyin: Chūntiān de gōngyuán lǐ dàochù shì huā.
examples.english: The park is full of flowers in spring.

examples.hanzi: 我最喜欢春天的天气。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ zuì xǐhuan chūntiān de tiānqì.
examples.english: I like spring weather the best.

components.note: 氵 (water) — muddy, mixed water; also in 河 river, 海 sea.
军 (jūn) is a loose sound clue; it also sounds out 挥 huī and 辉 huī.
身 (body) — a person's body with a rounded belly. As a radical it marks body words: 躺 lie down, 躲 hide, 躯 body.

example.hanzi: 跑完马拉松后他浑身都疼。
example.pinyin: Pǎowán mǎlāsōng hòu tā húnshēn dōu téng.
example.english: After finishing the marathon, his whole body ached.
example.fact: The soreness felt all over the body a day or two after intense exercise, known as delayed onset muscle soreness, is caused by microscopic tears in muscle fibers rather than lactic acid buildup, a myth that persisted for decades — lactic acid actually clears from the muscles within about an hour of exercise ending.

examples.hanzi: 他淋了雨，浑身都湿透了。
examples.pinyin: Tā lín le yǔ, húnshēn dōu shītòu le.
examples.english: He got caught in the rain and was soaked all over.

examples.hanzi: 我浑身没力气，想早点睡觉。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ húnshēn méi lìqi, xiǎng zǎodiǎn shuìjiào.
examples.english: I have no strength in my whole body and want to go to bed early.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — hand actions, as in 拿, 抱, 把; 打 is to hit.
丁 (dīng) is a loose sound clue for dǎ; 丁 also sounds out 订 dìng, 顶 dǐng and 钉 dīng.
扌 (hand, 提手旁) — hand actions; 搅 is to stir, as in 打 hit, 拉 pull.
觉 (jiào/jué) gives a close sound, as in 睡觉 shuì jiào.

example.hanzi: 抱歉打搅你了,我能问个问题吗?
example.pinyin: Bàoqiàn dǎjiǎo nǐ le, wǒ néng wèn gè wèntí ma?
example.english: Sorry to disturb you, may I ask a question?
example.fact: The 'Do Not Disturb' sign hung on hotel doorknobs is believed to date back to the early 20th century as hotels standardized guest privacy signals, and by the mid-1900s it had become such a universal fixture that some hotel chains began printing branded, novelty, or humorous versions as a form of guest amenity.

examples.hanzi: 对不起，打搅一下，请问洗手间在哪儿？
examples.pinyin: Duìbuqǐ, dǎjiǎo yíxià, qǐngwèn xǐshǒujiān zài nǎr?
examples.english: Excuse me for interrupting, where is the restroom?

examples.hanzi: 他在睡觉，请不要打搅他。
examples.pinyin: Tā zài shuìjiào, qǐng bú yào dǎjiǎo tā.
examples.english: He is sleeping, so please don't disturb him.

components.note: 亲 (qīn) keeps the sound part of the traditional 親, which also had 见; it also gives 新 xīn and 薪 xīn, so qīn/xīn is a series.
辶 (walk) — movement, as in 过, 远, 送: coming closer.
斤 (jīn) is a close sound clue for jìn.

example.hanzi: 这个孩子从小就跟爷爷很亲近。
example.pinyin: Zhège háizi cóngxiǎo jiù gēn yéye hěn qīnjìn.
example.english: This child has been close to his grandfather since childhood.
example.fact: Studies of attachment in early childhood, beginning with British psychologist John Bowlby's work in the 1950s, found that a secure, closely bonded relationship with at least one consistent caregiver in the first years of life is one of the strongest predictors of emotional resilience and healthy relationships later in adulthood.

examples.hanzi: 小狗很亲近主人。
examples.pinyin: Xiǎogǒu hěn qīnjìn zhǔrén.
examples.english: The puppy is very close to its owner.

examples.hanzi: 我们是亲近的朋友，什么都可以说。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen shì qīnjìn de péngyou, shénme dōu kěyǐ shuō.
examples.english: We are close friends and can talk about anything.

components.note: 争 (contend) — simplified from 爭, two hands pulling at the same object. See 战争 war and 竞争 compete.
讠 (speech, simplified 言) — talking and discussion: 说, 议, 谈; 论 is debate and theory.
仑 (lún) gives the sound; same part in 轮 lún and 伦 lún.

example.hanzi: 两位专家就这个问题展开了激烈的争论。
example.pinyin: Liǎng wèi zhuānjiā jiù zhège wèntí zhǎnkāi le jīliè de zhēnglùn.
example.english: The two experts engaged in a fierce debate over this issue.
example.fact: The Great Debate of 1920 was a formal astronomical dispute between Harlow Shapley and Heber Curtis over whether the Andromeda Nebula was part of the Milky Way or a separate, distant galaxy — the question wasn't settled until 1923, when Edwin Hubble measured Cepheid variable stars in Andromeda and proved it lay far outside our own galaxy.

examples.hanzi: 大家对这个计划没有争论。
examples.pinyin: Dàjiā duì zhège jìhuà méiyǒu zhēnglùn.
examples.english: Nobody argued about this plan.

examples.hanzi: 别为这点小事争论了。
examples.pinyin: Bié wèi zhè diǎn xiǎoshì zhēnglùn le.
examples.english: Stop arguing over such a small matter.

components.note: 人 (person) — a side-view figure of a person walking. As a radical it appears as 亻 on the left: 你 他 们.
攵 (tap, strike) — 攵 marks an action, here counting; as in 教, 放.
娄 (lóu) — loose hint — 数 is shù; 娄 also sounds out 楼 lóu.

example.hanzi: 参加会议的人数比预期多。
example.pinyin: Cānjiā huìyì de rénshù bǐ yùqī duō.
example.english: The number of people attending the meeting was more than expected.
example.fact: Woodstock, the 1969 music festival planned for an audience of about 50,000, ended up drawing an estimated 400,000 attendees — far exceeding food, water, and sanitation capacity — and the surrounding roads became so gridlocked that many performers had to be flown in by helicopter to reach the stage on time.

examples.hanzi: 今天来听课的人数不多。
examples.pinyin: Jīntiān lái tīngkè de rénshù bù duō.
examples.english: Not many people came to the lecture today.

examples.hanzi: 请告诉我你们班的人数。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng gàosu wǒ nǐmen bān de rénshù.
examples.english: Please tell me how many people are in your class.

components.note: 艹 (grass, plants) — flowers and growth: 花, 草, 茶; 荣 (from 榮) is a tree 木 in full bloom: flourishing, honor.

example.hanzi: 能在这里工作，我感到很荣幸。
example.pinyin: Néng zài zhèlǐ gōngzuò, wǒ gǎndào hěn róngxìng.
example.english: I feel very honored to work here.
example.fact: 荣 once meant a tree in bloom and developed into "glory": 荣幸 (honoured, a polite phrase), 光荣, 荣誉 (honour), 繁荣 (prosperous). It is also a surname.

examples.hanzi: 能认识你们，我感到很光荣。
examples.pinyin: Néng rènshi nǐmen, wǒ gǎndào hěn guāngróng.
examples.english: I feel honored to know you all.

examples.hanzi: 这个城市现在越来越繁荣。
examples.pinyin: Zhège chéngshì xiànzài yuè lái yuè fánróng.
examples.english: This city is getting more and more prosperous.

components.note: 回 (return) — a swirl or whirlpool drawn as nested squares: it turns around and comes back.
彐 (broom top, from 帚) — in the old form 歸 a woman with a broom 帚 'returns' to her husband's home; the story is a traditional account, not proven.
追 (zhuī) — the old form 歸 is said to use 追-like parts for sound; guī is only a loose match. Treat as a memory aid, not a rule.

example.hanzi: 每年秋天，大雁都会回归南方过冬。
example.pinyin: Měi nián qiūtiān, dàyàn dōu huì huíguī nánfāng guòdōng.
example.english: Every autumn, the wild geese return south for the winter.
example.fact: Atlantic salmon can swim thousands of kilometers back to the exact river where they hatched, guided partly by sensing Earth's magnetic field and partly by the unique chemical scent of their home stream. This precise homing ability, called natal river fidelity, remains one of the most striking examples of long-distance animal navigation.

examples.hanzi: 假期结束了，他回归了正常的生活。
examples.pinyin: Jiàqī jiéshù le, tā huíguī le zhèngcháng de shēnghuó.
examples.english: The holiday ended and he returned to his normal life.

examples.hanzi: 这位歌手宣布回归乐坛。
examples.pinyin: Zhè wèi gēshǒu xuānbù huíguī yuètán.
examples.english: The singer announced a return to the music scene.

meanings: abbr. for 公共汽車|公共汽车[gong1 gong4 qi4 che1]
car belonging to an organization and used by its members
abbr. for 公務用車|公务用车[gong1 wu4 yong4 che1]

components.note: 公 (public) — 八 over 厶: dividing 八 what is private 厶; so "shared, public, fair".
车 (cart) — simplified from 車, a wheeled cart seen from above. As a radical it marks vehicles: 转 turn, 轮 wheel, 较.

example.hanzi: 他每天坐公车去上班。
example.pinyin: Tā měitiān zuò gōngchē qù shàngbān.
example.english: He takes the bus to work every day.
example.fact: The world's first public bus-like service, the “carrosses à cinq sols,” began running fixed routes through Paris in 1662 at the urging of mathematician Blaise Pascal, charging a flat fare of five sols per ride. The venture folded within a few years, and organized urban mass transit did not reappear in a lasting form until the 19th century.

examples.hanzi: 公车来了，快上车吧。
examples.pinyin: Gōngchē lái le, kuài shàngchē ba.
examples.english: The bus is here, hurry up and get on.

examples.hanzi: 这条路线的公车每十分钟一班。
examples.pinyin: Zhè tiáo lùxiàn de gōngchē měi shí fēnzhōng yì bān.
examples.english: Buses on this route come every ten minutes.

components.note: 宀 (roof) — houses and shelter, as in 家, 字, 室.
女 (woman) — a woman at home under the roof: calm and safe.
玉 (jade) — jade put away safely: 全 first meant flawless, pure, then whole.
巾 (cloth) — cloth, as in 布, 帽, 帮: a belt of cloth with pieces hanging from it.

example.hanzi: 上车以后，请先系好安全带。
example.pinyin: Shàng chē yǐhòu, qǐng xiān jìhǎo ānquándài.
example.english: After getting in the car, please buckle your seat belt first.
example.fact: Swedish engineer Nils Bohlin invented the modern three-point seat belt in 1959 while working at Volvo, replacing the far less effective two-point lap belt. Volvo made the patent freely available to every other car manufacturer, a decision credited with saving hundreds of thousands of lives worldwide in the decades since.

examples.hanzi: 开车一定要系安全带。
examples.pinyin: Kāichē yídìng yào jì ānquándài.
examples.english: You must always wear a seat belt when driving.

examples.hanzi: 小孩坐车时也要扣好安全带。
examples.pinyin: Xiǎohái zuòchē shí yě yào kòuhǎo ānquándài.
examples.english: Children also need to buckle their seat belts in the car.

components.note: 州 (region) — a river 川 with small islands of land in it; 州 is a region, and also sounds out 洲 zhōu.
长 (long, grow) — simplified from 長, an old person with long hair. Read cháng "long" or zhǎng "to grow, elder".

example.hanzi: 加州州长将在明天发表演讲。
example.pinyin: Jiāzhōu zhōuzhǎng jiāng zài míngtiān fābiǎo yǎnjiǎng.
example.english: The governor of California will give a speech tomorrow.
example.fact: In 2003, California governor Gray Davis became only the second U.S. state governor in history to be removed through a recall election, made possible because California's constitution lets voters petition for a special election at any point in a governor's term. Arnold Schwarzenegger won the simultaneous replacement vote and was sworn in weeks later.

examples.hanzi: 州长今天参观了我们的学校。
examples.pinyin: Zhōuzhǎng jīntiān cānguān le wǒmen de xuéxiào.
examples.english: The governor visited our school today.

examples.hanzi: 那位州长是去年当选的。
examples.pinyin: Nà wèi zhōuzhǎng shì qùnián dāngxuǎn de.
examples.english: That governor was elected last year.

components.note: 人 (person) — three persons 人人人: a crowd. Also in 观众 audience, 大众 the public.

example.hanzi: 观众都站起来鼓掌。
example.pinyin: Guānzhòng dōu zhàn qǐlái gǔzhǎng.
example.english: The audience all stood up and applauded.
example.fact: 众 is three 人 stacked, a classic way to show "many." It builds 观众 (audience), 大众, 群众 (the masses), 公众 (the public), and the common phrase 众所周知 (as everyone knows).

examples.hanzi: 公园里聚集了很多群众。
examples.pinyin: Gōngyuán lǐ jùjí le hěn duō qúnzhòng.
examples.english: A lot of people gathered in the park.

examples.hanzi: 这位歌手受到大众的喜爱。
examples.pinyin: Zhè wèi gēshǒu shòudào dàzhòng de xǐ'ài.
examples.english: This singer is loved by the public.

components.note: 丹 (cinnabar) — an ancient picture of a mine with cinnabar in it; 丹 is red, as in 牡丹.
尼 (ní) — 尼 sounds out 泥 ní and 呢 ní; here it appears mostly in foreign names such as 丹尼.
斤 (axe) — the original idea was chopping with an axe, as in 新, 斩 chop, 断 break; today 斯 is mostly a sound-borrowing syllable sī in foreign names like 俄罗斯.

example.hanzi: 丹尼斯是我们公司新来的工程师。
example.pinyin: Dānísī shì wǒmen gōngsī xīn lái de gōngchéngshī.
example.english: Dennis is the new engineer at our company.
example.fact: Dennis Ritchie, a computer scientist at Bell Labs, co-created the Unix operating system in 1969 and then designed the C programming language in the early 1970s to help rewrite it. C went on to directly influence nearly every major programming language that followed, from C++ and Java to Python, making it one of the most consequential pieces of software ever written.

examples.hanzi: 丹尼斯会说一点儿中文。
examples.pinyin: Dānnísī huì shuō yìdiǎnr Zhōngwén.
examples.english: Dennis can speak a little Chinese.

examples.hanzi: 你把这份文件交给丹尼斯吧。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ bǎ zhè fèn wénjiàn jiāo gěi Dānnísī ba.
examples.english: Hand this document over to Dennis.

components.note: 巾 (cloth) — 巾 is a cloth radical, as in 帽 hat, 带 belt; 布 is cloth, and by extension to spread or announce, as in 宣布.
罒 (net, form of 网) — nets and catching: 罗, 罚, 罪; 置 first meant to set a net, then to place.
直 (zhí) is a near sound match for zhì; same part in 值 zhí and 植 zhí.

example.hanzi: 我们花了一个下午布置婚礼现场。
example.pinyin: Wǒmen huāle yí gè xiàwǔ bùzhì hūnlǐ xiànchǎng.
example.english: We spent an entire afternoon setting up the wedding venue.
example.fact: NASA's Mission Control Center in Houston was deliberately arranged in tiers, with flight controllers seated by function so information could flow upward from technical specialists to the flight director without anyone needing to shout across the room. That tiered layout, first used for the Gemini and Apollo missions, is still the basic model for mission control rooms today.

examples.hanzi: 我想把客厅布置得温馨一点儿。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎng bǎ kètīng bùzhì de wēnxīn yìdiǎnr.
examples.english: I want to decorate the living room to make it cozier.

examples.hanzi: 老师给我们布置了很多作业。
examples.pinyin: Lǎoshī gěi wǒmen bùzhì le hěn duō zuòyè.
examples.english: The teacher assigned us a lot of homework.

components.note: 上 (above) — a mark above a line, the mirror of 下 below.
十 (ten/cross) — the visible part; 升 once was a ladle measuring grain, then 'to rise'. The shape does not explain this. Memory aid: a ladle lifted high.

example.hanzi: 气温一直在上升，今天特别热。
example.pinyin: Qìwēn yìzhí zài shàngshēng, jīntiān tèbié rè.
example.english: The temperature has kept rising, and it's especially hot today.
example.fact: Mount Everest is still growing by roughly 4 millimeters a year because the Indian tectonic plate continues to push into and slide beneath the Eurasian plate, a collision that first raised the Himalayas around 50 million years ago. Precise GPS measurements placed on the summit in recent years have confirmed the peak's ongoing upward creep.

examples.hanzi: 今年的房价还在上升。
examples.pinyin: Jīnnián de fángjià hái zài shàngshēng.
examples.english: Housing prices are still rising this year.

examples.hanzi: 气球慢慢地上升到了空中。
examples.pinyin: Qìqiú mànmàn de shàngshēng dào le kōngzhōng.
examples.english: The balloon slowly rose into the air.

meanings: to do what one is told

components.note: 口 (mouth) — sound and speech, as in 吃, 唱, 问.
斤 (jīn, axe) is only a loose clue for tīng; the traditional 聽 had 耳 ear.
讠 (speech) — words and language, as in 说, 请, 谢; 话 is speech.
舌 (shé, tongue) fits the meaning (speaking) and is a loose sound clue for huà; also in 活 huó.

example.hanzi: 这只狗很听话，从不乱叫。
example.pinyin: Zhè zhī gǒu hěn tīnghuà, cóng bù luàn jiào.
example.english: This dog is very obedient and never barks without reason.
example.fact: Border collies are widely considered the most trainable dog breed, and one named Chaser learned to recognize the names of over 1,000 individual objects in tests run by researchers at Wofford College. Her handlers found she could correctly retrieve a specific toy by name even when it was mixed in with dozens of others she had never fetched that way before.

examples.hanzi: 你要听话，不要乱跑。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ yào tīnghuà, bú yào luàn pǎo.
examples.english: Be good and don't run around.

examples.hanzi: 他的孩子特别听话。
examples.pinyin: Tā de háizi tèbié tīnghuà.
examples.english: His child is especially obedient.

components.note: 攵 (tap, strike) — hand with stick, as in 教, 改, 放: to gather by force or hand.
丩 (jiū) is only a loose sound clue for shōu.
艹 (grass, plants) — 艹 is grass and plants, as in 花, 草, 菜; hiding under vegetation — 藏 is to conceal or store.
臧 (zāng) — near sound — 藏 is cáng; 臧 also sounds out 脏 zāng.

example.hanzi: 他从小就喜欢收藏邮票。
example.pinyin: Tā cóngxiǎo jiù xǐhuan shōucáng yóupiào.
example.english: He has loved collecting stamps since he was a child.
example.fact: Charles Darwin was an obsessive beetle collector as a young man, and his lifelong habit of cataloguing small variations between specimens later shaped the observational skills he brought to developing the theory of evolution by natural selection. He once reportedly popped a rare beetle into his mouth to keep his hands free for catching two more.

examples.hanzi: 我爸爸喜欢收藏旧硬币。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ bàba xǐhuan shōucáng jiù yìngbì.
examples.english: My dad likes collecting old coins.

examples.hanzi: 这篇文章很好，我先收藏起来。
examples.pinyin: Zhè piān wénzhāng hěn hǎo, wǒ xiān shōucáng qǐlái.
examples.english: This article is great, so I'll bookmark it first.

components.note: 尺 (chǐ, ruler) — the visible top part, as in 尺寸 size. 尽 simplifies 盡 and the shape does not explain 'use up'. Memory aid: measure it to the very end.
页 (head, page) — in traditional 頭 (豆 + 页): 页 is an old picture of a head, as in 顶, 领, 额. 头 dropped both parts.
大 (big) — the bottom. Memory aid: a big 大 body with two dots ⺀ like eyes above — the head, as in 头发. The dictionary's reading is loose.

example.hanzi: 沿着这条路走到尽头就是海边。
example.pinyin: Yánzhe zhè tiáo lù zǒu dào jìntóu jiùshì hǎibiān.
example.english: Walk along this road to the end and you'll reach the seaside.
example.fact: The Trans-Siberian Railway's main line runs 9,289 kilometers from Moscow to Vladivostok, making it the longest continuous railway line in the world. Crossing it end to end takes about a week of near-constant travel through eight time zones.

examples.hanzi: 隧道的尽头有一道亮光。
examples.pinyin: Suìdào de jìntóu yǒu yí dào liàngguāng.
examples.english: There is a light at the end of the tunnel.

examples.hanzi: 他走到了走廊的尽头。
examples.pinyin: Tā zǒudào le zǒuláng de jìntóu.
examples.english: He walked to the end of the corridor.

components.note: 鱼 (fish) — the old 魯 had fish on top; the meaning 'foolish, rash' is later and not about fish. 鲁 is mostly the state and surname Lu.
日 (sun) — at the bottom (from older 白). Memory aid: a fish gaping in the sun is dazed — hence foolish, rash.

example.hanzi: 他说话有点鲁莽。
example.pinyin: Tā shuō huà yǒudiǎn lǔmǎng.
example.english: He speaks a bit rashly.
example.fact: 鲁 is the short name for Shandong province, after the ancient State of Lu, home of Confucius. The same character gives 鲁莽 (reckless), the surname Lu, and the writer 鲁迅 (Lu Xun).

examples.hanzi: 他做事太鲁莽，容易出错。
examples.pinyin: Tā zuòshì tài lǔmǎng, róngyì chū cuò.
examples.english: He acts too rashly and easily makes mistakes.

examples.hanzi: 鲁迅是一位很有名的作家。
examples.pinyin: Lǔ Xùn shì yí wèi hěn yǒumíng de zuòjiā.
examples.english: Lu Xun is a very famous writer.

components.note: 氵 (water) — leaking liquid; also in 漏 leak, 流 flow.
世 (shì) is only a loose sound clue for xiè.
雨 (rain) — marks weather and moisture, as in 雪, 雷, 雾; 露 is dew.
路 (lù) gives the sound exactly: 露 lù (dew) or lòu (reveal).

example.hanzi: 公司担心客户的信息会被泄露。
example.pinyin: Gōngsī dānxīn kèhù de xìnxī huì bèi xièlòu.
example.english: The company is worried that customer information might be leaked.
example.fact: In 2016, an anonymous source leaked 11.5 million confidential documents from the Panamanian law firm Mossack Fonseca, an event now known as the Panama Papers. The files exposed how numerous world leaders and wealthy individuals used offshore shell companies to hide assets, triggering resignations and investigations in dozens of countries.

examples.hanzi: 请不要泄露这个秘密。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng bú yào xièlòu zhège mìmì.
examples.english: Please don't leak this secret.

examples.hanzi: 管道破了，煤气泄露了。
examples.pinyin: Guǎndào pò le, méiqì xièlòu le.
examples.english: The pipe burst and gas leaked out.

components.note: 氵 (water radical, 三点水) — liquids and flow: 河, 汤, 酒; 治 first meant controlling water, then governing and curing.
台 (tái) is only a loose sound hint; the same part is in 始 shǐ and 胎 tāi.
心 (heart) — feeling better; also in 想 think, 感 feel.
俞 (yú) gives the exact sound; it also sounds out 愉 yú and 逾 yú.

example.hanzi: 医生说这种病是可以治愈的。
example.pinyin: Yīshēng shuō zhè zhǒng bìng shì kěyǐ zhìyù de.
example.english: The doctor said this illness can be cured.
example.fact: Alexander Fleming discovered penicillin in 1928 almost by accident, after noticing that mold had killed off bacteria in a petri dish he had carelessly left uncovered. It took over a decade before Howard Florey and Ernst Chain developed methods to mass-produce the drug, and penicillin went on to save an estimated hundreds of millions of lives from bacterial infections that were previously untreatable.

examples.hanzi: 这种感冒一周就能治愈。
examples.pinyin: Zhè zhǒng gǎnmào yì zhōu jiù néng zhìyù.
examples.english: This kind of cold can be cured within a week.

examples.hanzi: 听音乐让我觉得很治愈。
examples.pinyin: Tīng yīnyuè ràng wǒ juéde hěn zhìyù.
examples.english: Listening to music feels really soothing to me.

components.note: 口 (mouth) — calling out; 夕 (evening) beside it: in the dark you cannot be seen, so you call your name.
片 (slice) — the right half of 木 split down the middle: a flat piece. See 版 bǎn (printing plate) and 牌 pái (card).

example.hanzi: 他递给我一张名片，上面印着他的职位。
example.pinyin: Tā dì gěi wǒ yì zhāng míngpiàn, shàngmiàn yìnzhe tā de zhíwèi.
example.english: He handed me a business card with his title printed on it.
example.fact: In Japan, the exchange of business cards, known as meishi, follows a strict etiquette in which the card is presented and received with both hands, held so the recipient can read it right away, and never written on or pocketed in front of the giver. Breaking these unwritten rules is considered a minor social misstep in Japanese business culture.

examples.hanzi: 这是我的名片，请多关照。
examples.pinyin: Zhè shì wǒ de míngpiàn, qǐng duō guānzhào.
examples.english: This is my business card, and I look forward to working with you.

examples.hanzi: 我的名片用完了。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ de míngpiàn yòng wán le.
examples.english: I've run out of business cards.

components.note: 革 (leather) — marks hides and straps, as in 鞋, 靴 boots, 鞭 whip; 勒 is to rein in or tighten.
力 (lì) is only a loose sound hint for lè.
糸 (thread, traditional of 纟) — silk and cord: 紧 tight, 系 tie; 索 is a twisted rope, seen in 线索 clue.

example.hanzi: 有人试图用照片勒索这位明星。
example.pinyin: Yǒurén shìtú yòng zhàopiàn lèsuǒ zhè wèi míngxīng.
example.english: Someone tried to blackmail the star using photographs.
example.fact: The 2017 WannaCry ransomware attack encrypted files on more than 200,000 computers across 150 countries in a single weekend, demanding Bitcoin payments to unlock them. It exploited a Windows vulnerability that had been stockpiled by the U.S. National Security Agency and leaked online just a month earlier, and it briefly crippled parts of the United Kingdom's National Health Service.

examples.hanzi: 骗子想勒索老人的钱。
examples.pinyin: Piànzi xiǎng lèsuǒ lǎorén de qián.
examples.english: The scammer tried to extort money from the elderly.

examples.hanzi: 他被人勒索了一大笔钱。
examples.pinyin: Tā bèi rén lèsuǒ le yí dà bǐ qián.
examples.english: He was blackmailed out of a large sum of money.

components.note: 大 (big person) — a person with a line above the head, marking the sky above; tiān = heaven, sky, day.
上 (above) — a mark above a line, the mirror of 下 below.

example.hanzi: 晚上天上挂满了星星。
example.pinyin: Wǎnshang tiānshàng guàmǎnle xīngxing.
example.english: The sky was full of stars at night.
example.fact: The aurora borealis, or northern lights, forms when charged particles from the solar wind collide with oxygen and nitrogen molecules high in Earth's atmosphere, exciting them enough to emit light. Oxygen collisions typically produce green or red light, while nitrogen tends to glow blue or purple, and the display is only visible because Earth's magnetic field funnels the particles toward the poles.

examples.hanzi: 天上有一朵很大的白云。
examples.pinyin: Tiānshàng yǒu yì duǒ hěn dà de báiyún.
examples.english: There is a big white cloud in the sky.

examples.hanzi: 天上不会掉馅饼。
examples.pinyin: Tiānshàng bú huì diào xiànbǐng.
examples.english: There's no such thing as a free lunch.

components.note: 阝 (mound, hill) — left-side 阝 is 阜 (mound), as in 阳, 院; 陌 is a path between fields, then unfamiliar.
百 (bǎi) — near sound — 陌 is mò.
土 (earth) — a green shoot pushing up from the ground: growth, birth, life. 生 also sounds out 性 xìng, 姓 xìng and 星 xīng.

example.hanzi: 在这座城市，我感到很陌生。
example.pinyin: Zài zhè zuò chéngshì, wǒ gǎndào hěn mòshēng.
example.english: I feel like a stranger in this city.
example.fact: Many migratory birds, including the European robin, can sense Earth's magnetic field through a light-sensitive protein in their eyes, allowing them to navigate across completely unfamiliar terrain during their seasonal journeys. Experiments have shown this magnetic sense can be disrupted by certain wavelengths of light and even by weak radio-frequency noise.

examples.hanzi: 刚到新学校，同学们都很陌生。
examples.pinyin: Gāng dào xīn xuéxiào, tóngxuémen dōu hěn mòshēng.
examples.english: I just arrived at the new school, and all the classmates are unfamiliar.

examples.hanzi: 不要和陌生人说话。
examples.pinyin: Bú yào hé mòshēngrén shuōhuà.
examples.english: Don't talk to strangers.

components.note: 冏 (bright/window) — the lower part; dictionary treats it as the 'bright' hint. Meaning 'trade, business' is better remembered as a market (商店).
口 (mouth) — dictionary radical, as in 吃 eat. Memory aid: a shop-keeper's mouth calling out prices; 商量 is to 'talk it over'.
土 (earth) — ground and place, as in 地, 城, 坐: a field or open space.
昜 (yáng) is the traditional sound part, a loose clue for chǎng; the same part is in 汤 tāng, 扬 yáng and 肠 cháng.

example.hanzi: 周末我们经常去商场逛街。
example.pinyin: Zhōumò wǒmen jīngcháng qù shāngchǎng guàngjiē.
example.english: On weekends, we often go window-shopping at the mall.
example.fact: The Southdale Center, which opened in Edina, Minnesota in 1956, is generally credited as the first fully enclosed, climate-controlled shopping mall in the world. Its Austrian-born architect, Victor Gruen, designed it to recreate the feel of a European town square indoors, though he later grew critical of how the mall format he pioneered reshaped American suburbs.

examples.hanzi: 这家商场一共有六层。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiā shāngchǎng yígòng yǒu liù céng.
examples.english: This shopping mall has six floors in total.

examples.hanzi: 商场里正在打折，人很多。
examples.pinyin: Shāngchǎng lǐ zhèngzài dǎzhé, rén hěn duō.
examples.english: There's a sale at the mall, and it's crowded.

components.note: 著 (zhù / zhe) — older form of 着: 艹 plant + 者 (zhě) as sound. 着 is a variant with 羊 over 目; neither part gives the 'in progress' sense.
目 (eye) — the bottom. The eye family: 看, 眼, 睛, 睡. In 着 it is only part of a variant shape. Memory aid: 睡着 — eyes 目 shut, asleep.
辶 (movement, road) — 辶 marks going and moving, as in 过, 进, 送; 迷 is losing one's way.
米 (mǐ) — near sound — 迷 is mí, the same syllable with a different tone.

example.hanzi: 弟弟最近对拼图特别着迷。
example.pinyin: Dìdi zuìjìn duì pīntú tèbié zháomí.
example.english: My younger brother has been especially fascinated with puzzles lately.
example.fact: During the Dutch “tulip mania” of 1636 to 1637, buyers became so fixated on rare tulip bulbs that a single bulb of the prized Semper Augustus variety reportedly traded for more than ten times the annual income of a skilled craftsman. Prices collapsed within weeks, and the episode is still cited as one of history's earliest recorded speculative bubbles.

examples.hanzi: 她对中国历史非常着迷。
examples.pinyin: Tā duì Zhōngguó lìshǐ fēicháng zháomí.
examples.english: She is fascinated by Chinese history.

examples.hanzi: 孩子们看魔术看得着迷了。
examples.pinyin: Háizimen kàn móshù kàn de zháomí le.
examples.english: The kids were captivated watching the magic show.

components.note: 回 (return) — a swirl or whirlpool drawn as nested squares: it turns around and comes back.
复 (fù) sounds out 腹 fù belly and 覆 fù cover; as a word it means again or to repeat, as in 恢复, 重复.

example.hanzi: 请尽快回复我的邮件。
example.pinyin: Qǐng jǐnkuài huífù wǒ de yóujiàn.
example.english: Please reply to my email as soon as possible.
example.fact: Because radio signals travel at the speed of light, a message sent to a rover on Mars takes anywhere from about 4 to 24 minutes to arrive depending on the planets' positions in their orbits, and a reply takes just as long to come back. Engineers at NASA account for this delay by having rovers execute pre-planned sequences of commands rather than waiting for real-time instructions.

examples.hanzi: 收到信息后，请及时回复。
examples.pinyin: Shōudào xìnxī hòu, qǐng jíshí huífù.
examples.english: After you get the message, please reply in time.

examples.hanzi: 他的身体已经回复正常了。
examples.pinyin: Tā de shēntǐ yǐjīng huífù zhèngcháng le.
examples.english: His body has returned to normal.

components.note: 當 (traditional) — 田 field under 尚 (shàng), 尚 being a loose sound hint for dāng. 当 keeps only a squashed top and a few strokes of it.
尚 (shàng) — the top part of 當; only a loose sound clue today. 当 is dāng (to act as, should) or dàng (appropriate).
日 (sun) — time and day, as in 早 early, 时 time, 明 bright; 晚 is when the sun is late.
免 (miǎn) is a close sound clue for wǎn; it also sounds out 勉 miǎn and 挽 wǎn.

example.hanzi: 演出结束后，当晚剧组就庆祝到很晚。
example.pinyin: Yǎnchū jiéshù hòu, dāngwǎn jùzǔ jiù qìngzhù dào hěn wǎn.
example.english: After the show ended, the cast celebrated late into that very night.
example.fact: The RMS Titanic struck an iceberg shortly before midnight on April 14, 1912, and sank in the early hours of April 15, with roughly 1,500 people dying in the frigid North Atlantic waters that same night. Investigations afterward found that the nearby ship California had spotted distress rockets but did not respond, a failure that led to major changes in maritime radio-watch rules.

examples.hanzi: 当晚我们就住在山脚下的小旅馆。
examples.pinyin: Dāngwǎn wǒmen jiù zhù zài shānjiǎo xià de xiǎo lǚguǎn.
examples.english: That night we stayed in a small inn at the foot of the mountain.

examples.hanzi: 他当晚就把报告写完了。
examples.pinyin: Tā dāngwǎn jiù bǎ bàogào xiě wán le.
examples.english: He finished writing the report that same evening.

components.note: 典 — a book 冊 set on a stand 丌, a revered text; hence canon, classic, as in 经典 classic and 字典 dictionary.
礻 (altar, spirit — form of 示) — rites and worship: 神 god, 祝 wish, 福 fortune; 礼 are ritual courtesies.

example.hanzi: 毕业典礼将在大礼堂举行。
example.pinyin: Bìyè diǎnlǐ jiāng zài dà lǐtáng jǔxíng.
example.english: The graduation ceremony will be held in the main hall.
example.fact: The modern Olympic torch relay was introduced at the 1936 Berlin Games, devised by German organizing committee official Carl Diem to link the ancient Games at Olympia with the modern revival. The tradition has continued at nearly every Olympics since, even though the ancient Greek Olympics themselves never actually featured any torch relay at all.

examples.hanzi: 开幕典礼上有精彩的表演。
examples.pinyin: Kāimù diǎnlǐ shàng yǒu jīngcǎi de biǎoyǎn.
examples.english: There was a wonderful performance at the opening ceremony.

examples.hanzi: 我们参加了朋友的结婚典礼。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen cānjiā le péngyou de jiéhūn diǎnlǐ.
examples.english: We attended our friend's wedding ceremony.

components.note: 马 (horse) — 马 is the horse radical, as in 骑, 驶; 驾 is to harness a horse, then drive.
加 (jiā) — same sound, different tone — 驾 is jià; 加 also sounds out 架 jià.
灬 (fire) — fire and heat, as in 热 hot, 点 dot, 黑 black: light shining.
昭 (zhāo) is a close sound clue for zhào; 昭 itself means bright.

example.hanzi: 他去年才拿到驾照。
example.pinyin: Tā qùnián cái nádào jiàzhào.
example.english: He only got his driver's license last year.
example.fact: New Jersey became the first U.S. state to require a license for all drivers in 1913, though early licenses were often issued with little more than a signature and a small fee, without any road test. Mandatory driving exams did not become common across the United States until the 1930s, decades after cars had already become widespread.

examples.hanzi: 考驾照要先学交通规则。
examples.pinyin: Kǎo jiàzhào yào xiān xué jiāotōng guīzé.
examples.english: To get a driver's license, you first learn the traffic rules.

examples.hanzi: 出门别忘了带驾照。
examples.pinyin: Chūmén bié wàng le dài jiàzhào.
examples.english: Don't forget to bring your driver's license when you go out.

meanings: to take part in a competition

components.note: 参 (cān) is a sound clue for 惨 cǎn and 掺 chān; the old shape pictured three stars.
贝 (cowrie) — money and value, as in 财, 货, 买: competing for prizes was once tied to offerings and stakes.

example.hanzi: 今年有上百个国家参赛。
example.pinyin: Jīnnián yǒu shàng bǎi gè guójiā cānsài.
example.english: This year, over a hundred countries are competing.
example.fact: The ancient Olympic Games began at Olympia in Greece in 776 BC and continued to be held every four years for nearly 1,200 years before Roman emperor Theodosius I banned them in 393 AD as part of a suppression of pagan festivals. That makes the ancient Games one of the longest-running organized sporting traditions in recorded history.

examples.hanzi: 这次比赛有十支队伍参赛。
examples.pinyin: Zhè cì bǐsài yǒu shí zhī duìwu cānsài.
examples.english: Ten teams are taking part in this competition.

examples.hanzi: 他受伤了，不能参赛。
examples.pinyin: Tā shòushāng le, bù néng cānsài.
examples.english: He's injured and can't compete.

components.note: 鸟 (bird) — marks birds, as in 鸡 chicken, 鹅 goose, 鸽 pigeon.
甲 (jiǎ) is only a loose clue, but 押 yā shares this part with the same sound as 鸭.
子 (child) — a picture of a baby with arms outstretched and legs bundled. As a suffix (孩子, 房子) it is a light noun ending.

example.hanzi: 池塘里有几只鸭子在游泳。
example.pinyin: Chítáng lǐ yǒu jǐ zhī yāzi zài yóuyǒng.
example.english: There are several ducks swimming in the pond.
example.fact: A duck's feathers stay dry in water because a gland near the base of its tail, called the uropygial gland, produces an oil that the duck spreads over its feathers while grooming. This waterproof coating, combined with tightly interlocking feather barbs, traps a layer of air next to the skin that also helps keep the bird insulated in cold water.

examples.hanzi: 晚饭我们吃了一只烤鸭子。
examples.pinyin: Wǎnfàn wǒmen chī le yì zhī kǎo yāzi.
examples.english: For dinner we ate a roast duck.

examples.hanzi: 小鸭子跟在妈妈后面游泳。
examples.pinyin: Xiǎo yāzi gēn zài māma hòumiàn yóuyǒng.
examples.english: The ducklings swim along behind their mother.

components.note: Memory aid: 业 looks like a row of upright posts on a base, like a shop sign or an old tool stand; 'business/trade' is the extended meaning. Origin is unclear, so no firm etymology.
人 (person) — the roof-like top. 余 absorbed 餘 (food left over); the shape no longer explains 'remainder'. Memory aid: a person with leftovers.
食 (food) — the old 餘 had the food part 饣; 余 is its sound part (yú), the same series as 除 chú, 徐 xú, 途 tú, with loose matches.

example.hanzi: 摄影只是他的业余爱好。
example.pinyin: Shèyǐng zhǐshì tā de yèyú àihào.
example.english: Photography is just his amateur hobby.
example.fact: Comet Hale-Bopp, one of the brightest comets of the 20th century, was discovered independently in 1995 by two amateur astronomers, Alan Hale and Thomas Bopp, both observing on their own time with backyard telescopes rather than as part of any professional survey. It remained visible to the naked eye for a record 18 months.

examples.hanzi: 她利用业余时间学习画画。
examples.pinyin: Tā lìyòng yèyú shíjiān xuéxí huàhuà.
examples.english: She uses her spare time to learn to paint.

examples.hanzi: 他是个业余摄影师，不是专业的。
examples.pinyin: Tā shì ge yèyú shèyǐngshī, bú shì zhuānyè de.
examples.english: He's an amateur photographer, not a professional.

components.note: 火 (fire) — fire and heat: 灯, 烧, 爆; 炸 is to explode or to fry.
乍 (zhà) sounds exactly like 炸; also in 诈 zhà, 作 zuò, 昨 zuó.
艹 (grass, plants) — 艹 marks plants — medicine was made from herbs, as in 药 and 草.
约 (yuē) — near sound — 药 is yào; 约 also sounds out 钓 diào.

example.hanzi: 工人用炸药炸开了这块岩石。
example.pinyin: Gōngrén yòng zhàyào zhàkāile zhè kuài yánshí.
example.english: The workers used explosives to blast open this rock.
example.fact: Swedish chemist Alfred Nobel invented dynamite in 1867 by stabilizing the notoriously unpredictable explosive nitroglycerin with an absorbent mineral called diatomaceous earth, making it far safer to transport and handle. The fortune he earned from dynamite and other explosives patents later funded the Nobel Prizes, established in his 1895 will.

examples.hanzi: 矿工们在山里使用炸药开路。
examples.pinyin: Kuànggōngmen zài shān lǐ shǐyòng zhàyào kāilù.
examples.english: The miners use explosives to clear a path in the mountains.

examples.hanzi: 炸药必须由专业人员保管。
examples.pinyin: Zhàyào bìxū yóu zhuānyè rényuán bǎoguǎn.
examples.english: Explosives must be kept by professionals.

components.note: 亻 (person) — person radical; 佳 describes a fine person, then anything good, as in 最佳.
圭 (guī) — loose hint — 佳 is jiā; 圭 also sounds out 挂 guà and 鞋 xié.

example.hanzi: 我们需要找一个最佳方案。
example.pinyin: Wǒmen xūyào zhǎo yí ge zuìjiā fāng'àn.
example.english: We need to find the best solution.
example.fact: 佳 is a formal "good": 最佳 (best), 佳肴 (fine dishes), 佳节 (festive holiday). 每逢佳节倍思亲 is a famous line by Tang poet Wang Wei about missing family on holidays.

examples.hanzi: 今天他的状态不佳。
examples.pinyin: Jīntiān tā de zhuàngtài bù jiā.
examples.english: He is not in good form today.

examples.hanzi: 这次比赛他取得了佳绩。
examples.pinyin: Zhè cì bǐsài tā qǔdé le jiājì.
examples.english: He achieved excellent results in this competition.

components.note: 宀 (roof) — houses and shelter, as in 家, 字, 室.
女 (woman) — a woman at home under the roof: calm and safe.
自 (nose) — over 心 heart: breath comes through the nose from the heart, so rest, news.

example.hanzi: 愿逝者在天堂安息。
example.pinyin: Yuàn shìzhě zài tiāntáng ānxī.
example.english: May the departed rest in peace in heaven.
example.fact: The ancient Parthian Empire, which controlled much of Persia and Mesopotamia from around 247 BC to 224 AD, was famous for a cavalry tactic later named the “Parthian shot,” in which mounted archers would feign retreat and then twist backward in the saddle to fire arrows at pursuing enemies. Roman armies suffered several major defeats, including at the Battle of Carrhae in 53 BC, before adapting to counter it.

examples.hanzi: 他的爷爷昨天安息了。
examples.pinyin: Tā de yéye zuótiān ānxī le.
examples.english: His grandfather passed away peacefully yesterday.

examples.hanzi: 愿你的亲人安息。
examples.pinyin: Yuàn nǐ de qīnrén ānxī.
examples.english: May your loved one rest in peace.

components.note: 口 (mouth) — calling out; 召 itself sounds out 招 zhāo, 照 zhào and 超 chāo.
刀 (dāo) is only a loose sound clue for zhào.
口 (mouth) — calling out loud; also in 叫 shout, 喊 yell.
奂 (huàn) gives the exact sound; it also sounds out 换 huàn, 焕 huàn and 痪 huàn.

example.hanzi: 号角声召唤士兵们回到营地。
example.pinyin: Hàojiǎo shēng zhàohuàn shìbīngmen huídào yíngdì.
example.english: The horn call summoned the soldiers back to camp.
example.fact: During World War I, both sides relied heavily on carrier pigeons to summon reinforcements or relay urgent messages when telephone lines were cut by shellfire. One pigeon, a hen named Cher Ami, was credited with delivering a message that helped save nearly 200 trapped American soldiers in 1918 despite being shot through the chest and leg during the flight.

examples.hanzi: 远方的山川召唤着旅行者。
examples.pinyin: Yuǎnfāng de shānchuān zhàohuàn zhe lǚxíngzhě.
examples.english: The distant mountains and rivers call out to travelers.

examples.hanzi: 他听到了内心的召唤。
examples.pinyin: Tā tīngdào le nèixīn de zhàohuàn.
examples.english: He heard the call of his heart.

components.note: 巴 (bā) — 巴 gives the sound bā in 爸 bà, 吧 ba, 把 bǎ and 疤 bā, so it is a useful sound clue.
士 (scholar, soldier) — usually read as an axe or weapon, so a warrior or gentleman (士兵, 博士). Memory aid: 士 has the longer bar on top, 土 (earth) on the bottom.

example.hanzi: 我们坐巴士去了机场。
example.pinyin: Wǒmen zuò bāshì qùle jīchǎng.
example.english: We took the bus to the airport.
example.fact: London introduced the world's first regular horse-drawn omnibus service in 1829, and by 1847 competing operators had begun stacking extra seating on the roof, creating the earliest double-decker buses. That basic two-level layout, later motorized, is still the design behind London's iconic red buses today.

examples.hanzi: 这辆巴士直接开到市中心。
examples.pinyin: Zhè liàng bāshì zhíjiē kāi dào shì zhōngxīn.
examples.english: This bus goes straight to the city center.

examples.hanzi: 我错过了最后一班巴士。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ cuòguò le zuìhòu yì bān bāshì.
examples.english: I missed the last bus.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — hand actions, as in 推 push, 拉 pull; 抵 is to push against.
氐 (dī) gives a close sound; it also sounds out 低 dī and 底 dǐ.
扌 (hand) — marks actions done by hand, as in 打, 推, 按; 抗 is to resist or hold off.
亢 (kàng) gives the sound exactly: 抗 kàng, also in 炕 kàng.

example.hanzi: 居民组织起来抵抗洪水。
example.pinyin: Jūmín zǔzhī qǐlái dǐkàng hóngshuǐ.
example.english: The residents organized themselves to resist the flood.
example.fact: Antibiotic resistance in bacteria arises through ordinary natural selection: when an antibiotic kills off most of a bacterial population, any cells carrying a random mutation that helps them survive the drug multiply freely and quickly dominate. The World Health Organization has identified this evolutionary process, accelerated by overuse of antibiotics in medicine and agriculture, as one of the top global public health threats.

examples.hanzi: 我们要增强体质来抵抗疾病。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen yào zēngqiáng tǐzhì lái dǐkàng jíbìng.
examples.english: We need to build our health to resist disease.

examples.hanzi: 他们没有抵抗，直接投降了。
examples.pinyin: Tāmen méiyǒu dǐkàng, zhíjiē tóuxiáng le.
examples.english: They didn't resist and surrendered directly.

components.note: 戈 (halberd, weapon) — war and weapons: 我, 成, 武, 伐; here fighting.
占 (zhàn) sounds exactly like 战; also in 站 zhàn and 粘 zhān.
術 (traditional) — 行 (road) plus 朮 (zhú) as sound: art, method. 术 is the sound part alone; same sound in 述 shù, as in 手术, 技术, 艺术.

example.hanzi: 教练在赛前调整了战术。
example.pinyin: Jiàoliàn zài sài qián tiáozhěngle zhànshù.
example.english: The coach adjusted the tactics before the match.
example.fact: The ancient Greek phalanx, a tight rectangular formation of soldiers holding overlapping shields and long spears, dominated Mediterranean warfare for centuries because it presented an almost unbroken wall of protection against any frontal attack. Its major weakness, exposed flanks and rear, was famously exploited by Theban and later Macedonian commanders who developed more flexible formations to outmaneuver it.

examples.hanzi: 这场比赛的战术很重要。
examples.pinyin: Zhè chǎng bǐsài de zhànshù hěn zhòngyào.
examples.english: Tactics are very important in this match.

examples.hanzi: 他们采用了新的战术。
examples.pinyin: Tāmen cǎiyòng le xīn de zhànshù.
examples.english: They adopted new tactics.

components.note: 亻 (person) — person radical — 传 is something passed from person to person.
专 (zhuān) — near sound — 传 is chuán; 专 also sounds out 转 zhuǎn and 砖 zhuān.
辶 (movement, road) — 辶 marks going and moving, as in 过, 进, 迷; 送 is walking someone off, or delivering.

example.hanzi: 这个软件可以快速传送文件。
example.pinyin: Zhège ruǎnjiàn kěyǐ kuàisù chuánsòng wénjiàn.
example.english: This software can transmit files quickly.
example.fact: On May 24, 1844, Samuel Morse sent the first long-distance telegraph message, “What hath God wrought,” from Washington, D.C. to Baltimore over a wire strung along a railway line. The demonstration proved that information could travel far faster than any horse or train, and telegraph networks expanded across the world within a few decades.

examples.hanzi: 他把照片传送给了远方的家人。
examples.pinyin: Tā bǎ zhàopiàn chuánsòng gěi le yuǎnfāng de jiārén.
examples.english: He sent the photos to his family far away.

examples.hanzi: 机场的传送带把行李送了出来。
examples.pinyin: Jīchǎng de chuánsòngdài bǎ xínglǐ sòng le chūlái.
examples.english: The airport conveyor belt delivered the luggage.

components.note: 人 (person) — a side-view figure of a person walking. As a radical it appears as 亻 on the left: 你 他 们.
才 (talent, just) — a sprout pushing out of the ground. 才 also sounds out 材 cái and 财 cái.

example.hanzi: 这家公司一直在寻找优秀人才。
example.pinyin: Zhè jiā gōngsī yìzhí zài xúnzhǎo yōuxiù réncái.
example.english: This company has always been looking for outstanding talent.
example.fact: Renaissance Florence, a city of perhaps 60,000 people, produced an extraordinary concentration of artistic talent, including Leonardo da Vinci, Michelangelo, and Botticelli, largely because wealthy families like the Medici competed to sponsor workshops, commissions, and apprenticeships. That patronage system gave promising young artists steady income and training that would have been unavailable in most other cities of the time.

examples.hanzi: 他是一位难得的人才。
examples.pinyin: Tā shì yí wèi nándé de réncái.
examples.english: He is a rare talent.

examples.hanzi: 我们公司很重视培养人才。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen gōngsī hěn zhòngshì péiyǎng réncái.
examples.english: Our company puts great emphasis on training talent.

components.note: 比 (side by side, to compare) — two people next to each other, as in 比较. The top part of 皆: 'all, together'.
白 (white) — the bottom; here probably a worn form of an older shape (自 'each'), not 'white'. Memory aid: everyone lined up in a row — all of them.

example.hanzi: 这件事人人皆知。
example.pinyin: Zhè jiàn shì rénrén jiē zhī.
example.english: Everyone knows about this.
example.fact: 皆 is a formal, written equivalent of 都 (all). Like 都, it comes before the verb. It features in idioms 皆大欢喜 (everyone is happy) and 比比皆是 (found everywhere).

examples.hanzi: 这里的风景皆美如画。
examples.pinyin: Zhèlǐ de fēngjǐng jiē měi rú huà.
examples.english: The scenery here is all as pretty as a picture.

examples.hanzi: 大家皆大欢喜。
examples.pinyin: Dàjiā jiē dà huānxǐ.
examples.english: Everyone is delighted.

components.note: 糸 (thread, traditional of 纟) — silk and cord: 紧 tight, 系 tie; 索 is a twisted rope, seen in 线索 clue.

example.hanzi: 我在网上搜索资料。
example.pinyin: Wǒ zài wǎng shàng sōusuǒ zīliào.
example.english: I search for information on the internet.
example.fact: 索 first meant a rope (绳索) and grew into "to look for" and "to demand": 搜索 (to search), 索引 (index), 索取 (to ask for), 线索 (clue, literally thread-rope). 索性 means "simply" or "might as well."

examples.hanzi: 警察正在搜索那个地区。
examples.pinyin: Jǐngchá zhèngzài sōusuǒ nàge dìqū.
examples.english: The police are searching that area.

examples.hanzi: 他向朋友索要一本书。
examples.pinyin: Tā xiàng péngyou suǒyào yì běn shū.
examples.english: He asked his friend for a book.
